name: Sweet tartlet shells (individual tart crusts)

recipe.title: Sweet tartlet shells (individual tart crusts)

ingredients.item: almond meal (ground almonds) (, not almond flour (Note 2))
ingredients.name: almond meal (ground almonds) (, not almond flour (Note 2))

ingredients.item: / 7 tbsp  unsalted butter (, unsalted, softened, cut into 1cm / 0.4" cubes)
ingredients.name: / 7 tbsp  unsalted butter (, unsalted, softened, cut into 1cm / 0.4" cubes)

directions: Mix dry ingredients, rub in butter then egg (or use food processor). Form disc, fridge 30 min. Portion into 6 balls*, roll out 15 cm / 6.5" round (~3mm / 1/8" thick), line 6 tartlet tins, trim excess. Fridge 30 min. Blind bake 12 min at 200°C / 390°F (180°C fan) with weights + 5 min uncovered for par-baked. * For mini tins or muffin tin, roll out single large one and press out circles. Gather scraps and repeat.

By hand option - Mix together flour, icing sugar, salt and almond meal in a bowl. Add butter and use your fingertips to rub it in until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg, mix with a rubber spatula until it becomes too hard to stir anymore, then use your hands to bring it together into a dough.

Food processor (30 sec) - Using the standard metal S blade, pulse the flour, icing sugar, salt and almond meal once just to combine. Add butter and pulse 3 to 4 times until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg and blitz for 15 to 20 seconds until it comes together into a dough.

Fridge 30 min - Turn dough out from the bowl or food processor onto a work surface. Knead lightly just to bring together into a smooth ball. Flatten into a 2cm / 0.8" thick disc. Wrap with cling wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Divide dough (for larger tartlet tins) - Cut the disc into 6 equal portions, or however many tartlet tins you are using, then roll into balls. (If using a muffin tin or lots of mini tart tins, don't portion, roll out one big sheet, press circles out and press into tin. See Note 4)
Roll each ball out into a 15 cm / 6.5" round (~3mm / 1/8" thick).

Line and trim - Press pastry into 6 tartlet tins (12cm / 4.7"), taking care not to stretch the dough as this causes shrinkage during baking. Roll the rolling pin over the tartlet tin to trim excess dough. (No need to grease the tins even if they are not non-stick ones, the butter in the pastry essentially self-greases the tins - as reader Ali so succinctly explained!).
Prick the base of the pastry 10 times with a fork. Not all the way through - just make a light prick on the surface. (Do less pricks for smaller tarts).
Refrigerate 30 minutes - Put the pastry in the tart tin for 30 minutes. (Extra insurance policy to avoid shrinkage and walls sliding down).
Preheat oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C fan-forced).

Baking beads - Cut or tear baking paper into pieces about 50% larger than the tart shells. Scrunch the paper in your fist then unravel, smooth out and fit into the tartlet tins (scrunching makes it fit in more easily into the corners). Fill with baking beads (or dry raw rice or beans).

Park-bake or fully baked? Par-bake if the tartlet shell will be baked again after filling (eg. almond cream / frangipane like Raspberry Tartlets). Fully bake if they will not be baked again (eg filling with pastry cream or whipped cream).

Par-baked (12 + 5 min) - Bake 12 minutes. Use paper overhang to remove the beads, then bake uncovered for 5 minutes. Pastry should pale golden on the base and light golden on the edges. It will go golden when the filled pastry is baked.
Fully baked (14 + 5 min) - Bake 15 minutes, remove beads, then bake 5 minutes uncovered. The base should be light golden and the edges should be golden.
Cool and fill - Fully cool in the tart tins before filling and baking again if filling needs to be cooked (like Raspberry Tartlets).
Storage - Or keep unfilled in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Aussie Lemon Coconut Slice Cake
name: Aussie Lemon Coconut Slice Cake

recipe.title: Aussie Lemon Coconut Slice Cake
recipe.description: Recipe video above. This is a lovely buttery lemon coconut cake topped with lemon icing and coconut, made for cutting into bars or squares and eating with hands. The icing crusts over, so it’s perfect for lunchboxes, gifting and transporting. And it keeps incredibly well - fresh for a week!You'll need one very large lemon or two regular lemons. You can leave out the coconut if you want, to make plain lemon. Gluten-free - See Note 3
ingredients: 1 cup plain flour / all-purpose flour ((Note 3 for gluten-free))
3/4 cup desiccated coconut (, unsweetened (Note 1))
1 tsp baking powder
1/8 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt
125g / 8 tbsp unsalted butter (, softened (Note 2))
3/4 cup white sugar (, caster/superfine or regular/granulated)
2 large eggs (, at room temperature (~50-55g/2 oz))
1 tbsp lemon zest
2 tbsp lemon juice (, at room temperature)
1 tsp vanilla
1/2 cup milk (, full fat, at room temperature)
2 cups soft icing sugar / powdered sugar (, sifted)
7 - 8 tsp lemon juice (, BE CAREFUL! Goes from perfect to runny with the teeniest amount too much!)
2 tbsp desiccated coconut (, for sprinkling)
directions: Whisk Dry, set aside. Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs one at a time. Beat in vanilla, zest and juice. On low, beat in 1/3 flour then 1/2 milk, repeat, finishing with flour. Finish mixing by hand. Bake in 20cm/8" lined pan 30 min at 180°C/350°F (160°C fan). Cool upside down, spread with icing, sprinkle with coconut.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced). Grease and line a 20cm/8" pan with paper.
Dry ingredients - Whisk the Dry ingredients in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Cream butter - Using a handheld electric beater, cream the butter and sugar in a separate bowl until it is smooth and fluffy, about 2 minutes (don't use a stand mixer, there is insufficient volume).

Eggs, lemon and vanilla - Beat in the eggs one at a time until smooth. Then add the vanilla, zest and lemon juice and beat just until combined. It will look a little curdled at this stage, that's ok, it comes together in the next steps.

Alternate flour and milk - Add 1/3 of the flour and beat on low until mostly mixed in. Add half the milk and beat just until incorporated. Repeat with another 1/3 of the flour, the remaining milk, then the remaining flour, mixing only briefly after each addition. Stop beating as soon as the flour disappears, then finish mixing by hand with a rubber spatula, making sure all the flour is mixed in. The batter should be like softly whipped cream - not runny, but not thick like peanut butter, with little lumps from the coconut.
Bake - Scrape batter into the cake pan and smooth the surface. Bake 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then cool upside down on a rack - we will ice the base as it's nice and flat. Fully cool before icing.
Spread with the Lemon Icing, all the way to the edge. Then sprinkle with coconut while wet, so it sticks. Let the icing set for 1 hour before slicing to serve!

Persevere! Put the icing sugar and lemon juice in a large bowl and use a rubber spatula to mix, using a smearing motion to combine until the glaze becomes a thick spreadable consistency like peanut butter (rather than the runny drippy kind). Be patient, it takes time to mix and assertive smearing to combine just a bit of lemon with lots of icing sugar! Only add extra lemon juice 1/2 teaspoon at a time if needed - glazes go from too thick to runny very easily!
